sections.overview: Lethrinus microdon Valenciennes, 1830 is a widespread Indo-West Pacific emperor, recorded from the Red Sea and East Africa through southern Asia to Japan and Papua New Guinea.
sections.identification: It is relatively elongate, bluish grey or brown, often with irregular dark blotches and sometimes three dark streaks radiating forward from the eye; it can reach about 80 cm.
sections.habitat: It occupies sandy bottoms near coral reefs, with records extending to about 80 m deep.
sections.diet: It feeds on fishes, crustaceans, cephalopods and polychaete worms.
sections.behavior: It swims in small schools, sometimes together with the closely related Lethrinus olivaceus.
sections.reproduction: In Palau, spawning has been recorded through much of the year during the first five days of the lunar month, near reef edges.
sections.ecology: Compared with Lethrinus laticaudis, which uses seagrass beds and mangroves as a juvenile, L. microdon is reported over sand close to reefs; both are exploited as food fish.
sections.conservation: FishBase lists a 2015 IUCN assessment of Least Concern.
